text: Hi, how's it going? I'm a big coffee lover, so I guess I'll start there. I can't really start my day without a cup of coffee, and this morning was no different. I had one before I came to take this test, and I'm already looking forward to another one once it's over. I work in IT, and my days are pretty busy. I live in an apartment, and I'm pretty much a homebody. In my free time, I like listening to music, playing computer games, and reading. So, yeah, that's me in a nutshell: coffee, music, and my computer. I'm happy to be here, and I hope I do well today!

Well, if I had to choose, my favorite room is the kitchen. I know that sounds a little weird, but let me explain. In the corner by the window, I set up my own little coffee station. I have a hand grinder, a drip kettle, and a shelf full of coffee beans from all over the world. The sunlight comes in every morning, and it feels like my own mini cafe. My friends joke that I spend more time there than anywhere else! Every weekend, I grind the beans by hand, and the smell fills the whole house. That's the moment I feel the most relaxed. I like it because it's simple, but it makes me really happy. For a coffee lover like me, it's heaven.

I take care of the housework myself. I'm in charge of the dishes, the trash, and the recycling. In Korea, you have to sort the trash carefully, so it takes some time. I also do the laundry and cook simple meals. And I have a secret helper: a robot vacuum! I bought it a couple of years ago, and it's a lifesaver. It cleans the floors every day while I'm at work. But it's not perfect. One day, it swallowed one of my socks, and it started making a horrible noise. I had to take the whole thing apart! I laughed about it later. Now I make sure nothing is on the floor before I leave. A clean house really makes me feel better.

When I was a kid, I lived in an old house with a big yard. The thing I remember most is the persimmon tree in the middle of the yard. Every fall, it was full of orange fruit, and we picked them with a long bamboo pole. My mom also dried red peppers on a straw mat in the yard, so the whole place turned red! And of course, with so many people around, the house was never quiet. In the winter, we gathered around the heated floor and ate roasted sweet potatoes. Now, I live in an apartment. It's warm, clean, and convenient, but I don't have a yard. I can't pick fruit from my own tree, and kids these days will never know that feeling. So, in a way, I miss the old house. But I wouldn't trade my warm, modern apartment. Both have their good points.

Korea is a small country, but it has lots of nature. About 70 percent of the land is mountains, so you can see one almost anywhere. The biggest one is Hallasan on Jeju Island, and Seoraksan is famous for its beautiful fall colors. We also have a lot of rivers. The Han River runs right through Seoul, and people love to picnic and ride bikes along it. As for lakes, we don't have many big natural ones, but there are a lot of man-made lakes and dams. And since Korea is a peninsula, we're surrounded by the sea on three sides. Where I live, I can see the ocean from my window. To be honest, I think Korea has a little bit of everything.

One place I'll never forget is Seongsan Ilchulbong on Jeju Island. My family took a trip there when I was about eleven. It's a huge volcanic crater that rises right out of the sea. We woke up at 4 a.m., which was brutal, and climbed up in the dark to see the sunrise. My family kept pushing me from behind, saying, "Hurry up!" I was out of breath, but when we reached the top, I was speechless. The sky turned orange and pink, and the sea went on forever. The crater was like a giant green bowl. I remember thinking, "Wow, nature is amazing!" That's why it's still one of my favorite places.

Not long ago, a friend and I went hiking on a mountain near my house. To be honest, I'm not much of a hiker. I'm more of an indoor guy. But my friend said, "The leaves look gorgeous right now!" So I gave in. The trail was steeper than I expected, and I was huffing and puffing after just ten minutes. My friend was way ahead of me, laughing the whole time. But when we got to the top, I couldn't believe my eyes. You could see the blue sea, small islands, and ships in the distance. We sat on a rock, drank hot coffee from a thermos, and just enjoyed the view. I have to admit, it was worth every step. Now I want to go back.

The healthiest person I know is my neighbor. She's in her sixties, but she has more energy than I do! She gets up at 5 every morning and goes for a walk up a small mountain near her house. She says it keeps her young. She also eats lots of vegetables, and she hardly ever eats fast food. When she invites us for dinner, the table is full of greens and soup. I always joke, "Where's the meat?" And she goes to bed early, by 9:30. I think that's why she looks so good. She's also a positive person, and she smiles a lot. Honestly, I think her happy mind is part of her secret. She's a great role model for me.

Yes, I tried something simple last year. I used to sit at my desk all day, even during lunch. My back started to hurt, and I felt tired all the time. So I made a small rule: take a 20-minute walk after lunch. I asked a coworker to join me, and we started walking around our building. At first, it felt like a chore. But after about two weeks, I noticed a big difference. I didn't get sleepy in the afternoon, and my back felt better. We also got to chat, so it was a nice break. Now it's become a habit. Even on rainy days, we walk inside the building. It proves that you don't need a fancy gym, just a little effort.

A couple of years ago, I got a wake-up call. I took my yearly health checkup at work, and the doctor said, "Your cholesterol and blood pressure are high." He told me I had to change my lifestyle or I'd be in trouble. That really shook me up. I thought about my family, and I wanted to stay healthy for them! So I signed up for a personal training program at a gym near my house. My trainer was a tough guy, and he made me work out three times a week. I also cut down on late-night snacks. After three months, I lost about five kilograms, and my numbers went down. I felt lighter and had more energy. It was hard at first, but it was one of the best decisions I've ever made.

Hello, I'm thinking about buying a new phone. I need one with a good camera, because I take a lot of pictures when I travel. I also need a long-lasting battery and plenty of storage. So, first, which models do you recommend?. Okay. How much storage do they have?. I see. And how good is the camera? Does it work well in the dark?. Got it. What about the price? Do you offer monthly payment plans?. One last thing: does the phone come with a warranty?. That sounds great. I'll stop by the store this weekend. Thank you so much!

Hello, I bought a phone from your store two days ago, and I have a bit of a problem. When I got home and started using it, I found out it only has 128 gigabytes of storage, and it doesn't have wireless charging. Those are two things I really need, because I take lots of pictures and videos and I charge my phone at my desk. I should have checked more carefully, but I'd like to exchange it for a better model. I still have the box and the receipt. Could I bring it in tomorrow after work? And is there a model with 256 gigabytes and wireless charging? I'm happy to pay the difference. Please let me know what time works for you. Thank you so much for your help!

Yes, I have one story about wireless earbuds. I read tons of reviews online, and everybody said the sound was incredible. The price was great too, so I ordered a pair without thinking twice. When they arrived, the music did sound great. But the thing is, the microphone was terrible. The first time I used them for a video call at work, my coworkers said, "Hey, you sound like you're in a tunnel!" I tried all the settings, updated the software, and even restarted them, but nothing worked. It was kind of embarrassing. So I contacted the seller and asked for a refund. They were nice about it, and I sent the earbuds back. I then bought a different brand in a store, so I could test them first. Lesson learned: reviews aren't everything!

I think there are a few reasons. First of all, people care a lot more about their health these days. Fifteen years ago, nobody counted calories. Now, everyone checks the label. If a restaurant only sells greasy food, they'd lose customers. Second, there's a lot of competition. Anyone can order from a hundred places on a delivery app, so restaurants have to stand out. A salad or a low-carb option is a good way to do that. Also, the younger generation loves eating clean and staying fit. A young coworker of mine is a good example. She always asks, "Is there a healthy option?" Even the government pushes it, by asking restaurants to show calories. So in the end, it's good for business. I think it's a win-win: people eat better, and restaurants make money.

Well, delivery has changed a lot lately. The biggest change is that you can get almost anything delivered. It used to be just chicken and Chinese food. Now, I can order a coffee, a salad, or even groceries with just a few taps. Another trend is single-serving meals. More people live alone, so restaurants offer small sets just for one. I've also noticed that delivery is faster than ever. Some stores promise to get it to you in 15 minutes! And there's more focus on the environment, with paper bags instead of plastic. Oh, and I've even seen robots delivering food in apartment buildings. Honestly, it feels like the future. I use delivery on weekends, and I love that it saves time. But I do miss the old days of eating out at the restaurant.
